newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher as funds buy, meal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher as funds buy, meal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended higher on Tuesday, boosted by commodity fund buying and commercial stopping of deliveries, traders said.
Soymeal ended mixed with nearbys down on a spread adjustment and on ideas Monday's rally was overdone.
"Most of it was spreading in the March/May. ADM stopped some oil and that generated some interest in the March," a trader said, referring to strength in soyoil.
Funds bought at least 2,000 lots of soyoil on the day. Merrill Lynch bought 700 lots July and 400 May, Griffin Trading bought 800 May and Smith Barney bought 600 July.
Commercials were sellers of soyoil on the day. ADM sold 700 lots May while Cargill Inc sold 500 May and bought 250 May. Produce Grain sold 300 lots each March and May.

A strike at Brazil's Paranagua port was seen a mildly supportive but a port spokeswoman told Reuters a strike would not affect loading of soymeal. Port operators said Tuesday afternoon the 72-hour strike would begin at 1200 local, 0900 CST Wednesday.
Soymeal ended $2.00 per ton higher to $0.90 lower with March off $0.90 at $262.30. Soyoil closed 0.38 to 0.15 cent per lb higher with March up 0.35 at 24.82.

On the day, ADM sold 200 lots March soymeal and 300 lots May. Cargill Inc sold 100 lots each March and May. Merrill Lynch sold 300 lots May and ING sold 200 May. LIT bought 100 March and 200 May, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 25,660 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 28,000 lots, against Monday's actual volume of 27,541 lots.
